scams.name: The Campo dei Miracoli Bracelet & Rose Ambush
scams.description: Along Via Santa Maria — the 500-metre tourist corridor from Pisa Centrale toward the Campo dei Miracoli — and on the lawn in front of the Leaning Tower, street vendors step into your path with 'a gift for you, my friend,' drop a woven string bracelet on your wrist or press a rose into your hand, then aggressively demand €5–€20 per piece. Firsthand r/rome, r/ItalyTravel and r/firenze reports repeatedly confirm the same MO is practiced at Pisa: 'I had one grab me at Pisa. I asked him not to touch me and he asked why. I told him I would punch him in the face.' 'They had this going on at the tower in Pisa. We just let it hit the ground.' Pisa Today's coverage of the city's new Polizia Turistica (launched 2026 from a new Piazza del Duomo sede) explicitly cites 'borseggi e abusivi' — pickpockets and unlicensed street vendors — on Piazza dei Miracoli as the problem the unit was created to address.
scams.avoidance: Never accept anything handed to you on Via Santa Maria or at the Campo dei Miracoli — not a bracelet, not a rose, not a pen. Walk past without stopping, without eye contact, without saying 'no grazie' (locals on r/rome warn that any response is treated as the start of a transaction). If an item lands on your wrist, let it fall to the ground and keep walking. If a vendor grabs your arm, loudly say 'polizia!' — the new Polizia Turistica post on Piazza del Duomo patrols the square. Keep children close: families are the preferred target.
scams.location: Via Santa Maria (train-station-to-Tower corridor), Piazza dei Miracoli lawn, Piazza del Duomo, the perimeter of the Battistero and Camposanto

scams.name: Piazza dei Miracoli Pickpocket Rings
scams.description: Pickpocket teams — including 'pregnant' women, clipboard-petition duos and children brushing past — work the Piazza dei Miracoli crowd in the exact seconds when tourists tilt their phones up for the 'holding the Tower' photo. A firsthand r/florence 'Pickpockets' thread documents the textbook attempt: 'In Pisa I felt a bump against me and immediately looked at my purse. It was open and my wallet was gone. I grabbed the pregnant lady that had bumped me and yelled you stole my wallet.' A La Nazione cronaca piece — 'Pisa, mordi e fuggi, ma occhio ai borseggi' — quotes guides warning tourists heading up Via Cammeo toward the square: 'marsupi, borse ben in vista e strette in mano, cerniere chiuse e occhi aperti, che qui spesso i turisti vengono derubati.' A separate Pisa Today report ('Turisti borseggiati alle stazioni ferroviarie') documents three women (two underage) stopped at San Rossore and an adult arrested at Pisa Centrale for furto aggravato — the same rings rotating between station and square.
scams.avoidance: Compose your Tower photo before you stop walking — phone out, back-pack swung to chest, zipper facing your sternum. Never wear a wallet in a back pocket at the Campo dei Miracoli; one r/Europetravel comment confirms 'pants with zip pockets aren't safe either' after a Pisa-Tower bus attempt. Treat any stranger who enters your arm's-length zone — 'pregnant' woman, clipboard petitioner, child, tour guide with a laminated badge — as a threat and step back one full pace. Call 112 immediately if robbed; the Polizia Turistica sede on Piazza del Duomo is a 30-second walk from the Tower.
scams.location: Piazza dei Miracoli lawn (Leaning Tower selfie zone), Via Cammeo, Via Santa Maria, Piazza dei Cavalieri, San Rossore rail station

scams.name: Pisa Centrale & LAM Rossa Bus Pickpockets
scams.description: Pisa Centrale station and the LAM Rossa bus line — the direct route from the station to Piazza dei Miracoli — are documented pickpocket hotspots. A Pisa Today cronaca report, 'Autobus: fermati i due borseggiatori della Lam Rossa,' describes police stopping two pickpockets working a LAM Rossa stop near the station 'with a furtive attitude, watching departing passengers.' La Nazione's 'Stazione, più poliziotti in borghese contro i borseggi' reports plainclothes officers deployed inside Pisa Centrale specifically to reduce 'lo sciame di borseggiatrici' (the swarm of pickpocketers). A TripAdvisor review of Pisa Central Station documents an active bus-transfer scam on tourists arriving day-trip. One r/florence traveller reports Pisa was the city where an attempted theft succeeded while an identical Rome metro attempt failed — the crowded 10-minute LAM Rossa ride is the decisive window.
scams.avoidance: At Pisa Centrale, exit via the front (Piazza della Stazione) and walk the 1.5 km to the Tower via Corso Italia, crossing the Arno at Ponte di Mezzo — you skip the LAM Rossa pickpocket window entirely, and Pisa's real centro is on that walk. If you do take the LAM Rossa, board with your backpack on your chest, zipper facing your body, and keep a hand on your bag for the full ride. Never carry a wallet in a jacket side pocket on the bus — crowded boarding is the moment. Tap-pay on the bus validator, not a third-party app (one r/ItalyTravel user was fined €45 in Pisa when Deutsche Bank tap didn't register). Buy tickets at the Autolinee Toscane kiosk inside Pisa Centrale, not from a 'helper' on the platform.
scams.location: Pisa Centrale station (platforms, ticket hall, forecourt), LAM Rossa bus stops near the station and along Viale Gramsci, San Rossore station

scams.name: The LAM Rossa "Unvalidated Ticket" €45 Shakedown
scams.description: Autolinee Toscane fare-checkers routinely fine tourists €40–€80 for 'invalid' tickets on the Pisa Centrale–Tower LAM Rossa bus, often on technicalities created by blocked validators and tap-pay systems that don't confirm in real time. A widely shared r/ItalyTravel post ('I actually really liked Pisa — then I met the fare checkers,' 148 upvotes) documents a pair of fare-checkers who physically blocked the ticket-stamper on the Tower-to-station bus, let the tourists stamp their tickets when they finally got through, then immediately fined them €80 for tickets they claimed had been stamped on the back previously — showing 'nothing on the back' as proof. A separate r/ItalyTravel 'Bus Fine - Pisa' thread documents a €45 fine for a Deutsche Bank tap-pay that didn't register in the checker's system, eventually resolved after weeks of emailing a PEC address. TripAdvisor reviewers repeatedly describe the same MO in 2024–2025: 'a huge problem happening in Pisa with bus transportation officials harassing tourists.'
scams.avoidance: Walk from Pisa Centrale to the Tower (1.5 km, ~20 min via Corso Italia and Ponte di Mezzo) — this removes the bus scam entirely and is the single most effective defense. If you take the LAM Rossa, buy a paper ticket at the Autolinee Toscane kiosk, stamp it in the yellow validator the moment you board (even if someone is 'blocking' the machine — politely force through), and photograph the stamped ticket with date and time visible. Prefer Apple Pay or Google Wallet over raw bank tap-pay — those confirm real-time. If fined, do not sign anything, do not pay on the spot, demand the fare-checker's ID (matricola) number and the Autolinee Toscane procedure to contest via PEC email — multiple travellers have had fines reversed this way.
scams.location: LAM Rossa bus (Pisa Centrale–Piazza dei Miracoli), Autolinee Toscane city buses, Pisa Centrale bus stop on Viale Gramsci

scams.name: Galileo Galilei Airport Unlicensed Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Unlicensed NCC operators and overcharging taxis at Pisa Galileo Galilei Airport — which sits 1.5 km from Pisa Centrale — have been flagged repeatedly by Italian press. Quinewspisa's 'Taxi e Ncc, segnalato abusivismo al Galilei' reports the taxi category publicly denouncing 'abusivismo e concorrenza sleale nel settore del trasporto persone, soprattutto nella zona dell'aeroporto Galilei.' Il Tirreno's 'Allarme abusivismo nel servizio taxi' names airport drivers as 'i più penalizzati tra i professionisti del trasporto regolare.' A separate Il Tirreno cronaca piece documents an unlicensed taxi driver caught shuttling tourists from Galilei to Livorno station — fined and banned — after 'years' of operating. A Facebook Italy-travel warning and multiple r/ItalyTravel comments confirm the pattern: 'Italian taxis are scams, source: i live here — there's a monorail from downtown pisa to the airport, should have taken that.'
scams.avoidance: Take the PisaMover automatic people-mover — a €5 ride (€2.70 tourist tariff inside the PisaAirport-to-Centrale package) that takes ~5 minutes between Pisa Airport and Pisa Centrale every 5–8 minutes from 06:00 to midnight. It beats any taxi on price, time, and scam risk. If you must take a taxi, use only the official white-painted CoTaPi vehicles at the signed rank outside Arrivi; confirm the meter is on tariff 1 (urban) before closing the door — the posted airport-to-centro rate is roughly €10–€15. Reject any 'taxi?' offers inside the terminal — those are abusivi. For Livorno, Pisa, or Lucca transfers, use Trenitalia direct from Pisa Centrale, not an airport driver quoting a 'flat fare.'
scams.location: Pisa Galileo Galilei Airport Arrivi forecourt, unofficial taxi rank, the stretch between the terminal and Pisa Centrale

scams.name: The Leaning Tower Car Park "Parking Official" Scam
scams.description: At the paid car parks serving the Leaning Tower — Parcheggio Pietrasantina (the official €3/hour coach and car lot on Via Pietrasantina) and unofficial overflow lots nearby — unlicensed parcheggiatori abusivi pose as parking attendants. They direct drivers into spots, demand cash 'parking fees' of €5–€20, sometimes issue fake hand-written 'receipts,' and pocket the money. A long-running TripAdvisor review — 'Beware of the car park scammers — Leaning Tower of Pisa' — warns explicitly that 'scammers operating in the Torre Di Pisa car park who purport to be parking officials' collect cash from tourists arriving by car. The variant: fake fee-collectors at the exit barrier claim the ticket machine is broken and demand cash to 'let you out.' Parcheggiatori abusivi are a crime under Italian law (Art. 7 comma 15bis Codice della Strada).
scams.avoidance: Use only Parcheggio Pietrasantina (the official €3/hour lot, 10-min walk from the Tower, pay at the automated ticket kiosk with card) or Parcheggio Via Paparelli — both are signed with Comune di Pisa brand and have machines, not humans, taking payment. If anyone in a yellow vest or plain clothes directs you to a spot and demands cash, they are a parcheggiatore abusivo — refuse, photograph them, and call 113. Never pay cash to any person in a Pisa parking lot. If you arrive by coach, use the dedicated bus parking at Pietrasantina, which is prepaid through your tour operator. Better: skip parking entirely and take the train to Pisa Centrale — all central Pisa is ZTL.
scams.location: Parcheggio Pietrasantina, unofficial overflow lots on Via Pietrasantina, Via Bonanno Pisano near the Porta Santa Maria wall, coach-parking zones north of the Campo dei Miracoli

scams.name: The Pisa ZTL Rental-Car Fine Trap
scams.description: Pisa's historic centre is a Zona a Traffico Limitato (ZTL) policed by automatic cameras that photograph every vehicle entering without a resident permit. Tourists driving rental cars from Galilei toward the Tower routinely cross ZTL lines unintentionally — signs are small, in Italian, and positioned after the point of no return. A documented r/legaladvice case ('Pisa Piazza Postal Problems') describes a driver who 'accidentally drove onto the pedestrian Piazza' on May 2, 2015 and received two €126 fines — one for entering, one for exiting — that arrived by mail a year later, with a €253 doubling when the international wire was disputed. A 2025 r/Scams thread documents five Avis emails invoicing €48 per 'police inquiry' fee to pass the driver's details on, in addition to the actual Comune fines (often €100–€200 each) from Rome, Florence, Pisa and Verona. r/florence travellers report: 'We received 2 tickets in the mail, about 6 and 8 months later.'
scams.avoidance: Do not drive into central Pisa. Park at Parcheggio Pietrasantina or return your rental to Pisa Centrale and walk — the Tower is 1.5 km away. If you must drive, download a Pisa ZTL map before leaving the airport and follow it literally — Via Roma, Piazza dei Miracoli and Via Santa Maria are all ZTL. Never trust Google Maps to route around ZTL: it will send you through one. If your hotel is inside the ZTL, email them 48 hours before arrival with your licence plate so they can register it with the Comune — this is legally required and must be done in advance. Budget for the Avis/Hertz/Europcar 'administrative fee' (typically €48) that is charged on top of every municipal fine passed along, and check your rental credit-card statement for six months after return.
scams.location: Central Pisa ZTL (Piazza dei Miracoli, Via Santa Maria, Piazza dei Cavalieri, Lungarno), the approach roads from Galilei Airport, Via Roma, Via Bonanno Pisano
